overall_summary: Analysis of the recent 16 videos shows that 'self respect' and boundary-setting topics (like muting chats, removing emergency contacts, or unpinning chats) consistently outperform generic late-night overthinking or raw sadness posts. View counts for self-respect pieces range higher (up to 38-40 views), whereas passive waiting tropes get lower traction. However, overall sample size is still small, so we must double down on the winning self-respect framework while reserving a small experiment budget for a fresh emotional angle.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'चैट डिलीट करने की हिम्मत' (40 views), 'ब्लू टिक्स आज छिपा दिए' (32 views), and 'स्टेटस लिस्ट में सबसे ऊपर उन्हीं का नाम था' (38 views) performed better than passive observational hooks.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on tangible digital boundaries (chats, statuses, block/unpin actions) rather than general feelings of loneliness.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing purely on time of night or unreturned texts like 'रात के दो बजे' (12 views) or 'मेज पर रखी चाय ठंडी हो गई' (5 views) show lower engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely atmospheric or passive waiting hooks unless paired with an empowering choice or self-respect twist.
